provenance.source: Halim, I., Zain, N. S., & Khoo, H. H. (2025). Assessing the feasibility of ammonia utilization for power generation: A techno-economic-environmental study. Applied Energy, 386, 125581. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.apenergy.2025.125581
provenance.how_read: Full text (15 pages) read; every page image holding a table, flowsheet or chart (pp. 1, 3-13) inspected and each number below checked against the page image. Supplementary material (Tables A1, A2) not available and not read.

status_key.verbatim: printed in the text or a table and confirmed on the page image
status_key.figure label: printed as a data label inside a figure, read from the page image
status_key.figure reading: read off a plotted curve; uncertainty stated
status_key.derived: arithmetic by this reader from printed numbers; formula in the note; not a number of the paper
status_key.absent: searched for in the whole text, every table and every figure and not found

provenance.page_note: Page numbers are the printed journal page numbers (1-15), which equal the PDF page numbers.
provenance.copyright_note: Numbers and short phrases only; no text or figure reproduced.

entries.value: 4 scenarios: (1) green NH3 cracked to H2, (2) blue NH3 cracked to H2, (3) green NH3 used directly as fuel, (4) blue NH3 used directly as fuel
entries.basis: costs per kg H2 or per kg H2-equivalent of fuel energy
entries.note: No fuel cell pathway. No partial-cracking-in-front-of-turbine pathway (unpurified H2/N2). No exhaust-heated cracker. The cracking pathway delivers purified H2 (PSA) that is co-fired with NH3.

entries.basis: electricity, vendor rating of the turbine (ref. [32], Mitsubishi Power H-25 web page)
entries.note: Stated as what the H-25 can generate 'up to'. Also the 'target power generation capacity' in the conclusions. Essay attribution located.
Not modelled. No turbine simulation, inlet conditions, pressure ratio or firing temperature are given.

entries.basis: not stated (LHV/HHV and fuel not stated); quoted from the vendor web page, ref. [32]
entries.note: Combined cycle. A vendor headline figure quoted, not computed. The paper does not say for which fuel; vendor ratings are normally for natural gas (not checked).

entries.quantity: H2 content the H-25 can operate on in NH3/H2 fuel mix
entries.basis: trade-press report, ref. [31] (POWER magazine, MHI/Mitsubishi Power breakthroughs, 2023)
entries.note: Essay attribution located. The paper relays a trade-press statement; it is a vendor-claim grade value, not tested in the paper.

entries.basis: energy content (LHV implied, see eta_implied)
entries.note: Derived check: 12,815.5 kg/h x 18.6 MJ/kg = 66.21 MW; 1,339.8 kg/h x 120.0 MJ/kg = 44.66 MW; NH3 share 59.7 % (60.0 % at LHV 18.8).

entries.basis: for 60.1 MW
entries.note: Equals 53 % NH3 / 47 % H2 by volume (printed; derived check 53.1 % NH3 with M = 17.031 and 2.016).
Table 3 note c gives furnace H2 output 1,815.7 kg/h; derived: 1,815.7 x (1 - 0.18 burned) x 0.90 PSA recovery = 1,340.0 kg/h, consistent with the product.

entries.value: Aspen Plus v14; PC-SAFT (cracking section); NRTL (NH3 recovery)
entries.note: Furnace as six RPLUG zones with heater blocks and calculator blocks (Fig. 2, p. 5); burner as Gibbs reactor; TSA and PSA as component separators (p. 7). Capital costs from Aspen Process Economic Analyzer (Table 3 note a).

entries.value: fired furnace burning 18 % of the furnace outlet gas (NH3 + H2 mixture, stream 5 split to stream 7)
entries.note: Fired by its own product gas, not by turbine exhaust. Combustion air preheated against flue gas. Excess air ratio 3.09.

entries.basis: stream 4
entries.note: 'approximately' 200 degC.

entries.basis: simulation
entries.note: Fig. 3 (figure reading): tube outlet about 500 degC, shell side about 1,370 degC at zone 6; uncertainty about +/-10 degC.

entries.basis: furnace outlet, excess air 3.09
entries.note: Outlet mass fractions NH3 0.207, H2 0.141, N2 0.652 (p. 5). Unconverted NH3 is absorbed in water and recycled (Section 2.3). Fig. 3 legend gives flame 1358.5 degC at excess air 3.09, 1377.6 at 3, 1400 at 2.9; the conversion curves overlap at about 80 %.

entries.value: Ru (3 wt%)-K (10 wt%)/CaO, fitted power law: k = 3807, Ea = 111, NH3 order 0.5, H2 order -1.2
entries.basis: fit to data of ref. [37] (Sayas et al. 2020)
entries.note: Furnace geometry in Table 1 (p. 5): 86 tubes, 0.04 m ID, 14 m tube height, 6 zones, catalyst density 3,350 kg/m3.

entries.quantity: Total energy required for H2 production by cracking
entries.basis: not stated (type of energy not broken down)
entries.note: Basis unclear; not used further here.

entries.value: water absorption of NH3 (T-101), then TSA (zeolite 4A, three beds, 10 bar, 61 degC) and PSA (zeolite 4A, 25 degC)
entries.note: TSA inlet gas 7.7 mol% NH3, 7.3 H2O, 21.2 N2, 63.7 H2. Recovered NH3 stream 97 mol% NH3; furnace feed 99.9 mol% NH3, < 800 ppm water. About 20 % of wash water purged.

entries.quantity: PSA H2 purity and overall recovery
entries.basis: literature value adopted, ref. [40]; modelled as a component separator
entries.note: Assumed, not computed.

entries.quantity: Utilities before and after heat recovery
entries.basis: Table 2 (before, after)
entries.note: The minus sign of K-101 (-284 kW, generation) confirmed on the image. Text p. 7 prints '284 kWh' for the same item (unit as printed). Text p. 7 says the network cuts cold utility by 91 % and hot by 96 %, and electricity from 2.48 to 2.28 kWh/kg H2 (8 %). Main load: adsorber compressor K-102 3,262 kW. Text p. 7 gives before-recovery demands of 8,220.2 kW cold, 6,140.5 kW hot, 3,328.1 kW electricity.

entries.quantity: Turbine efficiency used in the paper for both pathways
entries.value: 54 % (single value; same for NH3, H2 and their mix)
entries.basis: implied by the fuel flows (LHV) and by the equal-energy rule for the direct case
entries.note: Assumption, not computed. 60.1 MW / (66.21 + 44.66 MW) = 54.21 % at NH3 LHV 18.6 MJ/kg and H2 LHV 120.0 MJ/kg (53.86 % at 18.8; 53.97 % at the LHV 18.737 implied below). The paper never states an efficiency for any fuel separately and does not model the turbine.

entries.quantity: NH3 used directly in place of the cracked H2
entries.basis: same energy output as the H2 from the cracker
entries.note: Derived: 1,339.8 kg/h x 119.99 MJ/kg / 8,579.9 kg/h = 18.737 MJ/kg, i.e. NH3 LHV. Equal fuel energy for equal electricity means the paper assumes the same turbine efficiency on NH3 as on H2: delta = 0 pp on fuel basis (assumption).

entries.quantity: NH3 purchased for the cracking plant
entries.basis: Table 4 feedstock cost / price
entries.note: 102,126,100 USD / 944.20 USD/t = 108,162 t/yr; 43,043,900 / 397.96 = 108,161 t/yr; transport 4,542,800 / 42 = 108,162 t/yr (all three agree). Per hour at 8,760 h (the variable cost is multiplied by 0.9 in eq. 6). Checked against Fig. 5: 12,347.2 x 0.9442 / 1,339.8 = 8.70 USD/kg H2, the printed feed cost. The NH3 feed rate itself is not printed.

entries.quantity: NH3 LHV to product H2 LHV, cracking + PSA (paper's plant)
entries.note: 8,579.9 / 12,347.2 = 0.695. Includes the 18 % of cracked gas burned for heat, 80 % conversion with recycle and 90 % PSA recovery. AmCraX Aspen value for comparison: 87.7 % (turbine_threshold.json h1d_evidence).

entries.quantity: Electricity per NH3 LHV fed, whole 60.1 MW plant
entries.basis: AmCraX basis: NH3 LHV 18.60 MJ/kg; on LHV 18.737: 45.89, 53.97, -8.08

entries.quantity: Electricity per NH3 LHV fed, the 40 % H2 share only
entries.basis: turbine at 53.97 % on both fuels (implied)
entries.note: Electricity from H2 = 0.5397 x 1,339.8 x 119.99 / 3600 = 24.10 MW; / 12,347.2 kg/h = 1.952 kWh/kg; / 8,579.9 kg/h = 2.809 kWh/kg. With the paper's 69.5 % conversion, the H2 turbine would need to be 1/0.695 = 1.44 times as efficient as the NH3 turbine to break even on energy.

entries.quantity: H2-rich fuel turbine minus direct-NH3 turbine efficiency, same machine, fuel basis
entries.basis: LHV of fuel fed to the turbine
entries.note: Assumption of the paper (equal energy rule), not a sourced, computed, vendor or measured difference. Fuel is NH3 + 98 mol% H2 from PSA, not H2/N2 cracked gas.

entries.quantity: Discount rate, plant life, capacity factor
entries.basis: eq. (6)-(7); taken from ref. [21] (Makhloufi and Kezibri 2021)
entries.note: 0.9 appears as 8760 x 0.9 h in eq. (6); also applied to variable O&M. Derived CCF = 0.10608. CEPCI 800 (p. 7).

entries.basis: Aspen Process Economic Analyzer plus correlations; factors as % of PEC from ref. [21]
entries.note: Storage tank 25,000 t (cost from ref. [42]), about half of PEIC (derived 49.6 %); furnace about 40 % (derived 39.6 %; cost from ref. [43] Cesaro et al. 2021 for 1,815.7 kg/h H2). TCI = 580 % of PEC; 62 % direct, 25 % indirect, 13 % working capital (printed; derived 62.1, 24.8, 13.1). Turbine and power plant capital NOT included in any pathway.

entries.basis: Table 4
entries.note: Variable costs listed at 8,760 h and multiplied by 0.9 in eq. (6). Electricity 0.16 USD/kWh (50 % of residential 0.32, note c); derived 3,048.9 kW x 8,760 h x 0.16 = 4,273,338 USD.

entries.basis: Platts, July 2024, Middle East (ref. [48]); transport Middle East to Japan (ref. [49])
entries.page_or_table: Table 4 and notes a, b (p. 10); p. 7, p. 9
entries.note: Green FOB = 986.20 - 42. Blue 58 % below green (p. 9; derived 57.9 %).

entries.basis: eq. (6); cracking plant + storage, no power plant
entries.note: Fig. 5 labels: PEIC 0.72, other direct 1.04, indirect 0.70, working capital 0.37, O&M fixed 2.39, green NH3 8.70 (57.5 %), cargo 0.39, other variable 0.83. Derived reproduction from Tables 3-4: 15.147. Essay attribution located.

entries.basis: as above
entries.note: 33 % below green (printed; derived 33.1 %). Blue NH3 3.67 (36.3 %), O&M fixed 2.39 (23.7 %). Derived reproduction 10.113. Essay attribution located.

entries.basis: NH3 storage, vaporisation and compression only; 8,579.9 kg/h NH3
as above
entries.note: Feed 2.55 (44.5 %), O&M fixed 1.21 (printed '21.1' without a % sign in Fig. 5; text says 21.1 %).

entries.quantity: Direct NH3 use against cracking: cost reduction
entries.unit: % reduction of LCOA relative to LCOH
entries.basis: USD per kg H2 of fuel energy delivered to the turbine (1 - LCOA/LCOH); power plant excluded; equal turbine efficiency
entries.page_or_table: p. 1 Highlights ('reduces costs by 40 % versus cracking'); p. 9 (39 % green, 44 % blue)
entries.note: Derived: 1 - 9.2/15.1 = 39.1 %; 1 - 5.7/10.1 = 43.6 %. A fuel-cost comparison at turbine inlet for the 40 % H2 energy share only, NOT a levelised cost of electricity. The paper computes no LCOE.
Not computed for any pathway. No turbine or combined-cycle capital or O&M cost appears.

entries.quantity: Supply-chain GHG, NH3 delivered and cracked to H2 on Jurong Island
entries.basis: emission factors in supplementary Table A2 (not available); Saudi Arabia sources
entries.note: Fig. 6 labels (figure label): cracking plant 1.54 (blue) and 2.3e-1 (green); blue NH3 production at Jubail 2.58; alkaline electrolysis 3.97e-1; NG drilling 6.52e-1; NG dehydration 2.28e-1; Jurong storage 1e-1 (blue) and 1.51e-2 (green); cargo 2.79e-3 (7,806 km) and 3.15e-3 (8,849 km). Cracking-plant emissions differ for green and blue; the paper does not explain the basis.

entries.basis: life cycle of fuel supply; varies with H2 fraction 0-100 % (Fig. 7)
entries.note: Coal gasification (coal power, 90 % capture) exceeds the GEF at 73 % H2 or more (printed). Fig. 7 (figure reading, +/-0.01): coal line about 0.30 at 0 % H2 to 0.46 at 100 %; SMR about 0.19 to 0.29. Derived: per-kg-H2 to per-kWh conversion is about 18.0 kWh_e/kg H2 (5.21/0.289; 0.779/0.043), i.e. 33.33 kWh/kg x about 54 %.

entries.basis: levelised cost (USD/kg H2) / 33.33 kWh/kg H2, divided by NCA (GEF minus scenario emissions, kg CO2e/kWh)
entries.note: Minus signs (-0.044 NCA, -6.83 NCAC) confirmed on the image. Derived observation: the cost is put on a fuel-energy kWh (33.33 kWh/kg) while the NCA is per kWh of electricity; on an electricity basis (dividing by about 0.54) every NCAC would be about 1.85 times larger. The ranking is unchanged.

entries.basis: furnace flue gas of the cracker only; NO and NO2 computed by a Gibbs (equilibrium) reactor
entries.note: Implied mass derived: 466,000 / 4 = 116,500 kg NOx/yr (13.3 kg/h at 8,760 h). No NOx concentration printed. No turbine NOx for any fuel. N2O not mentioned anywhere.

entries.quantity: Carbon price or Singapore carbon tax
entries.note: No carbon tax or price is applied; the NCAC metric is used instead.

entries.value: (1) excess air 2.9 / 3 / 3.09 on flame temperature and conversion (Fig. 3); (2) GHG over water source, H2 and NH3 production route, energy source and H2 fraction 0-100 % (Fig. 7, Table 5); (3) green against blue NH3 price (scenarios)
entries.note: Section 3 is titled 'economic evaluation ... and sensitivity analysis', but no economic sensitivity on CAPEX, discount rate, capacity factor, turbine efficiency or scale is reported.

entries.value: no dynamic operation or supply-chain uncertainty (renewable availability, market fluctuation, supply disruption); no optimisation of the cracking plant
entries.note: Also: Singapore case; methodology said to be adaptable to Japan and South Korea (p. 3). Benchmark: electricity footprint 15 % above Makhloufi and Kezibri at 250 bar delivery (p. 7).

entries.value: turbine inlet conditions; turbine efficiency on any single fuel; efficiency basis of the 54 %; H2 delivery pressure to the turbine; NH3 feed flow of the cracker (only derivable from costs); power plant capital and O&M; LCOE; N2O; turbine NOx; cracker heat duty in MW; price year; stream table (supplementary Table A1); emission factors (Table A2)
